name: Oracle — CREATE TABLE by Unexpected Principal
description:
Attacker objective
Stage sensitive data for theft by copying tables (CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) before exfiltration.

Attack logic
CTAS in production is normally an ETL operation by a known service account. CREATE TABLE by any other principal — especially copying client or account tables — is data-staging behaviour.

Why this detection works
Unified Audit records the statement and principal, so allowlisting ETL makes other CTAS a high-signal event.

False positives
A new ETL/reporting account.

Tuning
Allowlist verified accounts; review the CTAS source table for sensitivity.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME, SQL_TEXT).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SQL_TEXT shows the CTAS source; copying sensitive client/account tables by an unexpected actor is data-staging for theft.
2. Correlate with any subsequent DB-link creation or large outbound transfer from the DB host.

name: Oracle — Dangerous ALTER SYSTEM Command
description:
Attacker objective
Weaken database security (disable auditing, change security parameters) or cause disruption via ALTER SYSTEM.

Attack logic
Routine ALTER SYSTEM in production is almost entirely session management (for example KILL SESSION) performed by a known service account. An ALTER SYSTEM that is not a kill-session, or is issued by a different principal, may be a parameter or security change.

Why this detection works
Unified Audit records the full statement text and the acting principal, so filtering out the routine session-management pattern isolates security-relevant ALTER SYSTEM.

False positives
A DBA legitimately changing a parameter during a maintenance window.

Tuning
Review SQL_TEXT; allowlist specific approved parameter changes or maintenance windows.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME, SQL_TEXT.keyword).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SQL_TEXT shows the exact command; a non-session-management ALTER SYSTEM (e.g. SET audit_trail, security params) is the concern.
2. Confirm change control and DBA authorisation.
false_positives: A DBA legitimately changing a parameter during a maintenance window.
query: ACTION_NAME.keyword:"ALTER SYSTEM" and (not USERNAME.keyword:"INH_LIFE" or (not SQL_TEXT.keyword:*KILL* and not SQL_TEXT.keyword:*kill*))

name: Oracle — Database Link Created by Unexpected Principal
description:
Attacker objective
Create a database link to an attacker-controlled or external database to exfiltrate banking data, or to pivot between systems.

Attack logic
Database links are an integration feature normally created by a known service account and pointed at known internal databases. A link created by any other principal, or one that points at an external/unknown host, is a potential exfiltration or pivot channel.

Why this detection works
Unified Audit records CREATE DATABASE LINK with the principal and statement text, so allowlisting the integration account and reviewing the target host turns link creation into a high-signal event.

False positives
A new legitimate integration account.

Tuning
Allowlist verified integration accounts; additionally review the USING clause (target host) for external addresses.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME, SQL_TEXT).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SQL_TEXT contains the link name and USING (target host); external or unknown targets indicate a likely exfiltration channel.
2. Drop the link if unauthorised and investigate the creating principal.
query: ACTION_NAME.keyword:"CREATE PUBLIC DATABASE LINK" and not USERNAME.keyword:"INH_LIFE"

name: Oracle DB — Database User Altered (Password/Privilege Change)
description: Detects ALTER USER operations on Oracle accounts (password reset, account unlock, privilege/profile change) — used for account takeover or persistence.
note:
## Investigation
1. `SQL_TEXT` shows what changed (IDENTIFIED BY = password change; ACCOUNT UNLOCK; GRANT).
2. Focus on changes to privileged accounts.
## Response
Reverse unauthorised changes; investigate.
author: raadabujaish

name: Oracle — DELETE by Unexpected Principal
description:
Attacker objective
Destroy banking records, or delete audit rows to cover tracks (anti-forensics), using SQL DELETE.

Attack logic
In a healthy core-banking database, DELETE activity is dominated by a small, fixed set of automated maintenance statements run by known service accounts. Interactive users and unknown principals do not routinely issue DELETE against banking or audit tables. The rule allowlists the sanctioned DELETE service accounts and alerts on DELETE by any other principal.

Why this detection works
Database Unified Audit records the action name and the acting principal for every statement, so an allowlist of sanctioned DELETE accounts turns any out-of-baseline DELETE into a single, high-signal event.

False positives
A newly introduced legitimate batch/service account that performs DELETE before it is added to the allowlist.

Tuning
Maintain the service-account allowlist and add verified batch/ETL accounts after change control. Optionally scope by target schema to also catch a sanctioned account deleting from an unexpected (production) table.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME/.keyword, SQL_TEXT).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the principal (USERNAME) and the target object (SQL_TEXT).
2. A DELETE against production banking or audit tables by a human or unknown account is high-risk.
3. Correlate with the account's session and prior activity; contain the account if unauthorised.
false_positives: A newly introduced legitimate batch/service account that performs DELETE before it is added to the allowlist.
query: ACTION_NAME.keyword:"DELETE" and not USERNAME.keyword:("BANKSYS" or "JCB_AML" or "BANKSBPM")

name: Oracle — New Principal Performing a Privileged Operation
description:
Attacker objective
A compromised or newly-created account begins performing privileged database operations (valid-account misuse / insider abuse).

Attack logic
Privileged database actions are performed by a small, stable set of service and admin accounts. The first time a principal not seen in the historical window performs a privileged action is a behavioural anomaly that complements the per-action rules.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the acting principal auto-baselines the known set from history and fires only on a genuinely new privileged actor.

False positives
Onboarding of a new legitimate service/admin account.

Tuning
Verify and allowlist new accounts; the history window auto-baselines over time.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the new principal and the privileged action performed.
2. Confirm whether the account was legitimately onboarded; if not, contain and investigate.
false_positives: Onboarding of a new legitimate service/admin account.
query: ACTION_NAME.keyword:("DELETE" or "TRUNCATE TABLE" or "ALTER SYSTEM" or "CREATE PUBLIC DATABASE LINK" or "CREATE TABLE" or "PL/SQL EXECUTE" or "CREATE USER" or "DROP TABLE")

name: Oracle — TRUNCATE TABLE by Unexpected Principal
description:
Attacker objective
Irrecoverably destroy data in banking tables. TRUNCATE is fast, minimally logged, and cannot be rolled back.

Attack logic
TRUNCATE in a core-banking database is normally limited to ETL/staging refreshes performed by a known service account against a fixed set of staging tables. TRUNCATE by any other principal is outside that pattern.

Why this detection works
Unified Audit captures the action and principal for every statement, so allowlisting the ETL account makes any other TRUNCATE a high-signal event.

False positives
A new ETL/maintenance service account not yet allowlisted.

Tuning
Allowlist verified ETL accounts. To also catch the ETL account truncating a production (non-staging) table, add an object allowlist scoped to the sanctioned staging tables.

Required telemetry
Oracle Unified Audit shipped as apps-* (ACTION_NAME, USERNAME, SQL_TEXT).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SQL_TEXT names the truncated table; confirm it is not a production banking table.
2. Confirm the actor is an authorised ETL principal.
3. If unauthorised, treat as data-destruction and begin IR.
false_positives: A new ETL/maintenance service account not yet allowlisted.
